To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in combination with conventional MR volumetry (CMR) is a useful tool for the assessment of complete tumor response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer.

the combination of conventional MR volumetry and diffusion-weighted MR (DW-MR) imaging is superior to conventional MR volumetry alone for the assessment of complete response (CR) after preoperative combined radiation with chemotherapy in rectal cancer.

the use of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in rectal cancer patients treated with preoperative combined radiation and chemotherapy is a promising method for the assessment of complete tumor response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for assessing complete response of rectal cancer to preoperative combined chemoradiotherapy based on diffusion-weighted MR (DW-MR) imaging.
the development of an MR-compatible device for the measurement of rectal wall thickness in patients undergoing radiotherapy.
the development of a novel method for the detection of the 3-D diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in the presence of a single-layered imaging (DW).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of diffusion-weighted MRI is a promising method to assess tumor response after preoperative combined radiation with chemotherapy.
the role of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in the evaluation of rectal cancer patients treated by preoperative combined radiation and chemotherapy is still under investigation.

the diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) technique can be used for rectal tumor staging, but it has to be combined with conventional MRI.
